countries.name: United States
countries.didYouKnow: The United States has the world's oldest written national constitution still in use, ratified in 1788.

hard: This country has 50 internal administrative divisions, each with its own legislature.
It invented the internet, the telephone, and the airplane within a 100-year span.
Its southern border is defined almost entirely by a single river.
medium: It contains the world's oldest national park, established in 1872.
More languages are spoken here than in any country in Europe.
Its national bird was nearly replaced by the wild turkey, according to one founding father.
easy: Its capital city is NOT its largest city.
It is bordered by only two countries, one to the north and one to the south.
Its national symbol is a bald eagle.

countries.name: France
countries.didYouKnow: France is the most visited country in the world, attracting around 90 million tourists per year.

hard: This country once controlled territory spanning five continents simultaneously.
It has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other European nation.
Its legal system became the template for dozens of countries after a famous emperor exported it.
medium: It produces over 1,000 distinct types of cheese.
Its national celebration on July 14th commemorates the storming of a famous prison.
The metric system was invented here during its revolution.
easy: Its capital is the most visited city in the world.
It is famous for its wine, fashion, and cuisine.
Its flag is a vertical tricolour of blue, white, and red.

countries.name: Germany
countries.didYouKnow: Germany has over 1,500 different types of beer and around 1,300 breweries.

hard: This country was divided into two separate states for 45 years before reunification.
It has the largest economy in Europe and the fourth largest in the world.
Its constitution, adopted in 1949, was specifically designed to prevent the rise of authoritarian rule.
medium: It shares borders with nine different countries — more than any other European nation.
Its annual autumn festival celebrating beer draws millions of visitors to one city.
The printing press was invented here in the 15th century.
easy: It is famous for its autobahn highway system, parts of which have no speed limit.
Its capital was a divided city for decades, separated by a famous wall.
Its flag is three horizontal stripes of black, red, and gold.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.didYouKnow: Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas.

hard: This country contains roughly 60% of the world's largest tropical rainforest.
It is the only country in South America that does not have Spanish as an official language.
Its capital was purpose-built from scratch in the late 1950s and opened in 1960.
medium: It has won the FIFA World Cup more times than any other nation.
The Amazon River, the world's largest by discharge, flows through it.
It is home to the world's largest carnival celebration, attracting millions annually.
easy: It is the largest country in South America by both area and population.
A giant Christ statue overlooks its most famous city from a hilltop.
Its flag is green and yellow with a blue celestial globe.

countries.name: Japan
countries.didYouKnow: Japan has around 6,800 islands, but the vast majority of the population lives on just four of them.

hard: This island nation experiences around 1,500 earthquakes per year due to its tectonic position.
It was the only country to suffer atomic bomb attacks, in 1945.
Its writing system uses three distinct scripts simultaneously: two phonetic and one pictographic.
medium: Its bullet train network, launched in 1964, remains one of the world's most punctual rail systems.
It has the world's highest life expectancy and a rapidly aging population.
Cherry blossom viewing is a national cultural tradition with festivals held every spring.
easy: It is an archipelago nation in the Pacific Ocean.
Mount Fuji, its iconic volcano, is visible from its largest city on a clear day.
Its flag is a simple red circle on a white background.

countries.name: Australia
countries.didYouKnow: Australia is the only continent that is also a single country, and it is home to more venomous species than any other nation.

hard: This country has more wild camels than any other nation — a result of 19th century imports gone feral.
Its indigenous population has the longest continuous cultural history of any people on Earth, exceeding 50,000 years.
It is the world's largest exporter of coal and iron ore.
medium: It is both a country and a continent.
The Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral system, runs along its northeastern coast.
Its capital was chosen as a compromise between its two rival largest cities.
easy: It is home to kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus.
It is located in the Southern Hemisphere, meaning its seasons are opposite to Europe's.
The Sydney Opera House is one of the most recognizable buildings in the world.

countries.name: Canada
countries.didYouKnow: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world at over 202,000 kilometres.

hard: This country has two official languages enshrined in its constitution.
It contains 20% of the world's fresh water supply.
Its northern territory includes parts of the Arctic Circle where the sun does not set for months.
medium: It is the second largest country in the world by total area.
Ice hockey is considered its national winter sport and a core part of cultural identity.
It shares the world's longest undefended border with its southern neighbour.
easy: Its national symbol, the maple leaf, appears on its red and white flag.
It is famous for maple syrup, producing 71% of the world's supply.
It is located directly north of the United States.

countries.name: Italy
countries.didYouKnow: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country in the world, with 58 listed sites.

hard: This country contains two independent states entirely within its borders.
It unification as a modern nation only occurred in 1861 — relatively recent for a European country.
It is shaped like a boot and is surrounded by five different seas.
medium: Its ancient empire once controlled territory from Britain to Mesopotamia.
It is the birthplace of opera, the Renaissance, and pizza.
Its fashion capital hosts one of the world's four major fashion weeks.
easy: It is famous for its pasta, pizza, and espresso.
The Colosseum, one of the ancient world's greatest structures, stands in its capital.
Its flag is a vertical tricolour of green, white, and red.

countries.name: Spain
countries.didYouKnow: Spanish is the world's second most spoken native language, and Spain exported it to over 20 countries.

hard: This country once controlled the largest empire in history by some measures, spanning the Americas, Africa, and Asia.
It has 17 autonomous communities, each with significant self-governing powers — some with their own official languages.
It is the second largest country in the European Union by area.
medium: Its most famous unfinished building has been under construction since 1882 and is still incomplete.
Its national sport involves a matador and a bull in an arena.
The Running of the Bulls festival is held here every July.
easy: Flamenco dance and guitar are iconic cultural exports of this country.
It occupies most of the Iberian Peninsula.
Real Madrid and FC Barcelona, two of the world's most famous football clubs, are based here.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.didYouKnow: Mexico City is built on the ruins of Tenochtitlan, the ancient Aztec capital, and sinks about 10 cm per year.

hard: This country is the 11th most populous in the world and the most populous Spanish-speaking nation.
It was home to the Aztec and Maya civilizations, whose ruins are still visited by millions.
It is one of the world's most biodiverse countries, ranking 5th globally.
medium: Its cuisine — including tacos, mole, and guacamole — is recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.
It borders three countries: two to the north and one to the south.
Day of the Dead is a nationally celebrated holiday unique to this country's cultural traditions.
easy: It is the largest Spanish-speaking country in the world by population.
It shares its northern border with the United States.
Its flag features an eagle on a cactus devouring a snake.

countries.name: China
countries.didYouKnow: China invented paper, printing, gunpowder, and the compass — four inventions that transformed human civilization.

hard: This country has the most international land borders of any nation, sharing borders with 14 countries.
Its economy overtook Japan's in 2010 to become the world's second largest.
It operates under a one-party political system that has been in continuous power since 1949.
medium: Its iconic ancient defensive structure stretches over 21,000 kilometres.
It is the world's largest manufacturer and exporter of goods.
Its writing system uses thousands of characters, each representing a word or concept.
easy: It is the most populous country in the world — or was until recently.
The giant panda is its national animal and a global symbol of wildlife conservation.
Its flag is red with a large yellow star and four smaller ones.

countries.name: India
countries.didYouKnow: India has over 1,600 dialects and languages spoken across the country, with 22 officially recognized ones.

hard: This country launched a mission to Mars for less money than the Hollywood film Gravity cost to produce.
It has the world's largest democracy, holding elections involving over 900 million eligible voters.
Chess, the number zero, and the decimal system are all believed to have originated here.
medium: It is the world's largest producer of milk, spices, and tea.
Its film industry, based in Mumbai, produces more films annually than any other country.
The Himalayan mountain range runs along its northern border.
easy: The Taj Mahal, one of the Seven Wonders of the World, is located here.
It recently surpassed China to become the world's most populous country.
The sacred River Ganges flows through its heartland.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.didYouKnow: The United Kingdom has never had a written constitution — it operates on a system of conventions, statutes, and common law.

hard: At its peak, this country's empire covered 24% of the Earth's land surface.
It is a constitutional monarchy made up of four distinct constituent countries.
The industrial revolution began here in the late 18th century, changing the world forever.
medium: English, the world's most widely spoken second language, originated here.
It voted to leave a major political union in a 2016 referendum, a process nicknamed after itself.
Shakespeare, Newton, Darwin, and the Beatles all came from this country.
easy: It consists of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
The Queen's Guard in red tunics and bearskin hats is one of its most famous images.
It drives on the left side of the road.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.didYouKnow: Ancient Egypt lasted over 3,000 years — longer than the gap between Cleopatra's time and today.

hard: This country controls one of the world's most strategically vital artificial waterways.
Its capital is the largest city in Africa and the Arab world.
It was among the first countries to sign a peace treaty with Israel, in 1979.
medium: The Nile, the world's longest river, flows through it from south to north.
Papyrus, one of the earliest writing materials, was invented here.
Its ancient rulers built tombs that are among the last remaining wonders of the ancient world.
easy: The Great Pyramids of Giza are one of its most iconic landmarks.
It is located in the northeastern corner of Africa, bordering the Mediterranean and Red Sea.
The Sphinx, a massive limestone statue, stands guard near its most famous monuments.

countries.name: Russia
countries.didYouKnow: Russia spans 11 time zones — when it's midnight on its western border, it's already midday on its eastern coast.

hard: This country contains Lake Baikal, which holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.
It was the first country to send a human to space, in 1961.
Its Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world at over 9,000 kilometres.
medium: It spans two continents and 11 time zones.
Its famous winter contributed to the defeat of both Napoleon and Hitler.
The Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 transformed it into the world's first communist state.
easy: It is the largest country in the world by land area.
Its iconic onion-domed cathedral sits on Red Square in the capital.
Vodka and matryoshka dolls are among its most famous cultural exports.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.didYouKnow: Argentina has produced five Nobel Prize winners — the most of any Latin American country.

hard: This country claims sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, which it went to war over in 1982.
It is the eighth largest country in the world by area.
Patagonia, one of the world's most remote and dramatic landscapes, occupies its southern third.
medium: It is the birthplace of tango, both the music and the dance.
It is one of the world's leading producers of beef and soy.
Its capital has the widest avenue in the world — 16 lanes across.
easy: It produced Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona, two of football's greatest players.
It is the second largest country in South America.
Its flag features a sun with a face, called the Sun of May.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.didYouKnow: South Africa is the only country in the world to have voluntarily dismantled its nuclear weapons program.

hard: This country has three capital cities — one legislative, one executive, and one judicial.
It is the world's largest producer of platinum and chromium.
It hosted both the FIFA World Cup in 2010 and the Rugby World Cup in 1995, both historic firsts for the continent.
medium: Its apartheid system of racial segregation ended in 1994 with its first fully democratic election.
Nelson Mandela, who spent 27 years in prison, became its first Black president.
It has 11 official languages — more than almost any country on Earth.
easy: It is located at the southern tip of the African continent.
The Big Five — lion, elephant, buffalo, leopard, and rhino — are found in its national parks.
Cape Town and Johannesburg are its most famous cities.

countries.name: Greece
countries.didYouKnow: Greece has more archaeological museums than any other country in the world.

hard: This country is considered the birthplace of democracy, philosophy, and the Olympic Games.
It has around 6,000 islands, of which only about 200 are inhabited.
Its language has been in continuous use for over 3,000 years, the longest of any European language.
medium: Its ancient myths — featuring Zeus, Athena, Poseidon, and Hercules — have influenced Western culture for millennia.
It joined a major economic union in 1981 and later required a historic financial bailout from it.
The Parthenon, sitting on its most famous hilltop, is one of the most recognized ancient structures.
easy: It is a Mediterranean country made up of a mainland and thousands of islands.
The ancient Olympics were first held here.
Its flag is blue and white with a cross in the corner.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.didYouKnow: About one-third of the Netherlands lies below sea level, kept dry by an elaborate system of dikes and pumps.

hard: This country engineered nearly 20% of its entire landmass out of the sea.
It was the first country in the world to legalize same-sex marriage, in 2001.
Its colonial trading company, the VOC, was the world's first publicly traded corporation.
medium: It is famous for tulip cultivation, windmills, and an elaborate canal network in its capital.
It is one of the world's largest exporters of agricultural products despite its small size.
Anne Frank hid from the Nazis in a secret annex in its capital city.
easy: Windmills, tulips, wooden clogs, and cycling are its most iconic cultural images.
It is a small, flat country in Western Europe known for its liberal social policies.
Its flag is a horizontal tricolour of red, white, and blue.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.didYouKnow: Sweden has the world's oldest national park outside of North America and over 800 nature reserves.

hard: This country was one of the most feared military powers in Europe during the 17th century.
It has not participated in any war for over 200 years, one of the longest periods of peace for any nation.
The Nobel Prize, awarded annually in most categories here, was established by one of its citizens.
medium: IKEA, Spotify, H&M, and Minecraft all originated in this country.
It has one of the world's highest gender equality rankings and parental leave policies.
The northern third of the country lies within the Arctic Circle.
easy: It is a Scandinavian country known for its Viking heritage and social welfare system.
ABBA and IKEA are two of its most globally recognized exports.
Its flag is a yellow cross on a blue background.

countries.name: Turkey
countries.didYouKnow: Istanbul is the only city in the world that straddles two continents — Europe and Asia.

hard: This country's territory is split between two continents by a narrow strait that connects two major seas.
It is home to the site of Troy, made famous by Homer's Iliad.
It controls the Bosphorus Strait, one of the world's most strategically important waterways.
medium: Its largest city is divided by water into a European side and an Asian side.
It contains more ancient Greek ruins than Greece itself.
Its most famous historical building was a church, then a mosque, then a museum, then a mosque again.
easy: It bridges the continents of Europe and Asia.
The whirling dervish, a form of spinning Sufi meditation, originated here.
Its flag features a white crescent moon and star on a red background.

countries.name: Poland
countries.didYouKnow: Poland was the first country in Europe to adopt a written constitution, in May 1791 — the second written national constitution in history after the USA.

hard: This country was erased from the map entirely for 123 years, partitioned among three neighbouring empires.
It lost approximately 17% of its population during World War II — the highest percentage of any country.
Marie Curie, the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, was born here.
medium: Its Solidarity trade union movement in the 1980s was a major catalyst for the collapse of communism in Europe.
It has the largest economy in Central and Eastern Europe.
Pierogi, kielbasa, and borscht are among its most well-known traditional foods.
easy: It is located in Central Europe, bordered by Germany to the west and Russia to the northeast.
The Auschwitz concentration camp, now a museum and memorial, is located here.
Its flag is two horizontal stripes — white on top and red on the bottom.

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.didYouKnow: Ukraine is the largest country located entirely within Europe by land area.

hard: This country contains Chernobyl, the site of the world's worst nuclear disaster in 1986.
It is known as the 'breadbasket of Europe' for its vast fertile agricultural plains.
Its capital was one of the most important cities in medieval European history.
medium: It is the largest country located entirely in Europe.
Its flag colors represent a blue sky above golden wheat fields.
It gained independence in 1991 when the Soviet Union dissolved.
easy: It has been at the centre of a major military conflict since 2022.
Its capital city is Kyiv.
Its flag is two horizontal stripes of blue and yellow.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.didYouKnow: Saudi Arabia has no rivers or permanent lakes — its water comes entirely from aquifers and desalination plants.

hard: This country has no permanent rivers or natural lakes despite being the size of Western Europe.
It controls roughly 17% of the world's proven petroleum reserves.
It is the only country with a flag that features writing — a religious declaration and a sword.
medium: It is home to Islam's two holiest cities, which millions of Muslims are obligated to visit once in their lifetime.
Women were not permitted to drive in this country until 2018.
It is governed by an absolute monarchy from the founding royal family.
easy: It occupies most of the Arabian Peninsula.
Mecca and Medina, the holiest cities in Islam, are located here.
It is the world's largest oil exporter.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.didYouKnow: South Korea has the fastest average internet speeds in the world and one of the highest smartphone penetration rates.

hard: This country went from one of the world's poorest nations to a high-income economy in a single generation — a transformation called its 'Miracle.'
It has mandatory military service for all male citizens.
It is home to some of the world's largest conglomerates including a company that makes phones, ships, and insurance.
medium: K-pop and K-dramas have become global cultural phenomena originating from this country.
It shares a heavily fortified border with one of the world's most isolated nations to the north.
Its capital is home to over half the country's total population in its metropolitan area.
easy: BTS and Blackpink are among the most globally famous music acts from this country.
It is located on a peninsula in East Asia.
Its flag features a red and blue Yin-Yang symbol on a white background.

countries.name: Thailand
countries.didYouKnow: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never colonized by a European power.

hard: This country is the world's second largest exporter of rice and a major producer of rubber.
It was formerly known by a name meaning 'Land of the Free.'
It is the only Southeast Asian nation that was never colonized by a European power.
medium: It is a constitutional monarchy where the royal family is held in extremely high reverence by law.
Muay Thai, a combat sport using fists, elbows, knees, and shins, was developed here.
Its most sacred temple in the capital contains a famous Emerald Buddha statue.
easy: It is one of the most visited countries in the world for tourism.
Pad thai, green curry, and mango sticky rice are among its most famous dishes.
Elephants hold deep cultural significance in this Southeast Asian country.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.didYouKnow: Nigeria produces more films per year than any country except India, a film industry known as Nollywood.

hard: This country has over 500 distinct ethnic groups and speaks more languages than any other African nation.
It is Africa's largest economy, driven largely by oil production and a massive services sector.
Its population is projected to surpass the United States by 2050.
medium: It is the most populous country in Africa.
Its film industry, nicknamed after Hollywood, is the second most prolific in the world.
It is one of the world's leading oil producers, with the Niger Delta being a major production zone.
easy: It is the most populous country in Africa, with over 200 million people.
It is located in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea.
Its flag is two vertical green stripes with a white stripe in the middle.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.didYouKnow: Kenya's Great Rift Valley is considered the cradle of humanity — some of the oldest known human fossils were found there.

hard: This country straddles the equator yet has a highland interior that experiences cool temperatures year-round.
It is the dominant global power in long-distance running, particularly marathons and 1500m events.
It hosts one of the world's greatest wildlife spectacles — the annual migration of over a million wildebeest.
medium: Its famous national reserve shares its name with the Maasai people who have herded cattle there for centuries.
Nairobi, its capital, is one of Africa's few cities with a national park visible from its skyline.
It produces some of the world's most prized tea and coffee.
easy: It is famous for its safari wildlife, including lions, elephants, and giraffes.
It is located on the eastern coast of Africa, on the Indian Ocean.
The Great Rift Valley, a massive geological trench, runs through it.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.didYouKnow: Colombia is the only country in South America with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

hard: This country is the world's leading producer of high-quality emeralds.
It has coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
Gabriel García Márquez, the Nobel-winning author of One Hundred Years of Solitude, was born here.
medium: It is the world's third largest producer of coffee, known for its rich mountain-grown beans.
Its biodiversity is second only to Brazil, with the most bird species of any country on Earth.
Shakira and Sofia Vergara are among its globally recognized celebrities.
easy: It is the world's second largest producer of coffee after Brazil and Vietnam.
It is named after Christopher Columbus.
Cumbia and vallenato are among its most famous traditional music styles.

countries.name: Chile
countries.didYouKnow: Chile is home to the driest non-polar desert on Earth — the Atacama — where some areas have never recorded rainfall.

hard: This country is the world's largest producer of copper, supplying roughly 28% of global output.
It is the longest country in the world from north to south — stretching over 4,300 kilometres.
Easter Island, home to the famous Moai stone statues, is its territory despite being in the middle of the Pacific.
medium: It contains the Atacama Desert, the driest place on Earth outside of the polar regions.
It is one of only five countries in the world with a Mediterranean climate type.
Its southern region, Patagonia, is shared with its eastern neighbour and known for dramatic glaciers.
easy: It is an extremely long and narrow country running down the western coast of South America.
The Andes mountain range forms its eastern border.
It is famous for its wine production in fertile central valleys.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.didYouKnow: Portugal is the oldest nation-state in Europe with its borders almost unchanged since 1139.

hard: This small country once controlled a maritime empire stretching from Brazil to Japan, pioneering the Age of Exploration.
Vasco da Gama, who discovered the sea route to India, was born here.
Its melancholic folk music genre, fado, is recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.
medium: It is the westernmost country in mainland Europe.
It exports port wine, cork (producing over 50% of the world's supply), and custard tarts.
It sent explorers who mapped the coasts of Africa, India, Brazil, and Japan in the 15th–16th centuries.
easy: It occupies the western portion of the Iberian Peninsula.
It colonized Brazil, which is why Brazilians speak Portuguese.
Its flag is split vertically into green and red, with a complex coat of arms.

countries.name: Romania
countries.didYouKnow: Romania's Transfăgărășan Highway, carved through the Carpathian mountains, has been called the world's most spectacular road.

hard: This country's orphanage crisis after 1989 shocked the world and led to widespread international adoptions.
It has the largest building in Europe by floor area — a massive palace constructed by its communist dictator.
Its gymnast Nadia Comaneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history in 1976.
medium: It is home to Transylvania, the region that inspired the legend of Count Dracula.
It has the largest gold reserves in Central and Eastern Europe.
Its language is a Romance language descended directly from Latin, making it distinct among its Slavic-speaking neighbours.
easy: Dracula's castle — Bran Castle — is located in its Transylvania region.
It is located in southeastern Europe, bordering the Black Sea.
Its flag is three vertical stripes of blue, yellow, and red.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.didYouKnow: Vietnam is the world's largest exporter of cashews and the second largest exporter of coffee.

hard: This country's iconic bay, with over 1,600 limestone islands, was formed by millennia of erosion and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
It defeated three superpowers militarily in the 20th century: Japan, France, and the United States.
It is the world's third largest exporter of rice.
medium: Its S-shaped coastline runs for over 3,000 kilometres along the South China Sea.
Pho, banh mi, and spring rolls are among its most internationally recognized dishes.
Its most famous landmark is a bay dotted with thousands of dramatic limestone pillars.
easy: It is a Southeast Asian country shaped like a long, narrow 'S.'
It fought a major war against the United States that ended in 1975.
Motorbikes vastly outnumber cars in its busy cities.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.didYouKnow: Indonesia has the world's second longest coastline and is the largest archipelago nation on Earth.

hard: This country sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and has over 130 active volcanoes.
It is the world's largest Muslim-majority country by population.
The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, one of history's deadliest disasters, devastated its northwestern shores.
medium: It consists of over 17,000 islands and is home to more than 300 distinct ethnic groups.
Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizards, are found only on a few of its islands.
Bali, one of the world's most visited tourist destinations, is one of its islands.
easy: It is the world's largest archipelago, made up of over 17,000 islands.
It is the fourth most populous country in the world.
Bali is its most famous island, known for temples, rice terraces, and beaches.

countries.name: Pakistan
countries.didYouKnow: Pakistan has more glaciers outside the polar regions than any other country — over 7,000.

hard: This country has the world's second highest concentration of glaciers outside of the poles.
It was created in 1947 as a homeland for Muslims during the partition of British India.
It is home to K2, the world's second highest mountain, considered more dangerous to climb than Everest.
medium: Karachi, its largest city, is one of the most populous cities in the world.
It became the world's seventh nuclear-armed state when it tested weapons in 1998.
The ancient city of Mohenjo-daro, one of the oldest civilizations in the world, is located here.
easy: It is an Islamic republic in South Asia.
It shares a border with India, Afghanistan, Iran, and China.
Its flag is green with a white crescent and star — and a white stripe on the left.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
countries.didYouKnow: Azerbaijan was the first country in the Muslim world to grant women the right to vote, in 1918.

hard: This country's capital contains three skyscrapers designed to resemble flames, visible for miles at night.
It sits at the crossroads of Eastern Europe and Western Asia and borders five countries.
It controls the Nagorno-Karabakh region, over which it fought two wars with a neighbouring country.
medium: Its capital sits on the Caspian Sea, the world's largest landlocked body of water.
It has been known as the 'Land of Fire' for millennia due to naturally occurring surface oil fires.
It is part of the South Caucasus region and shares cultural ties with Turkey.
easy: It is a former Soviet republic located between Russia, Iran, and the Caspian Sea.
Its capital city is Baku.
Its flag has three stripes — blue, red, and green — with a white crescent and eight-pointed star.

countries.name: Belarus
countries.didYouKnow: Belarus is one of the few countries that still retains significant Soviet-era iconography, including a modified version of the Soviet flag.

hard: This landlocked country has been described as 'Europe's last dictatorship' and has been led by the same man since 1994.
It was disproportionately devastated in World War II, losing about a quarter of its population.
It is one of the few countries in the world that has maintained a Soviet-style state economy.
medium: It is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe, bordered by Russia, Ukraine, Poland, and the Baltic states.
Its capital was almost entirely rebuilt in the Soviet architectural style after being destroyed in WWII.
It shares the closest cultural, linguistic, and political ties with Russia of any former Soviet republic.
easy: It is a landlocked former Soviet republic in Eastern Europe.
Its capital city is Minsk.
Its flag features a distinctive red and green horizontal stripe with a traditional decorative pattern.

countries.name: Bolivia
countries.didYouKnow: Bolivia is one of only two landlocked countries in South America, and it has two capitals — one constitutional and one administrative.

hard: This country is home to the Salar de Uyuni, the world's largest salt flat, which contains over half the world's known lithium reserves.
It has two capital cities — one serves as the seat of government and one as the constitutional capital.
Its main capital is the highest major city in the world at over 3,600 metres above sea level.
medium: It is a landlocked country in South America that lost its ocean access in a war in the 1880s.
Lake Titicaca, the world's highest navigable lake, sits on its border with Peru.
Its population is majority indigenous, making it unique among South American nations.
easy: It is a landlocked South American country known for its dramatic Andean landscapes.
The Salar de Uyuni, the world's largest salt flat, is located here.
Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world, is on its border.

countries.name: Cambodia
countries.didYouKnow: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument ever constructed, covering over 400 square kilometres.

hard: This country's population was reduced by roughly 25% under a radical communist regime in the 1970s.
The temple complex here is the largest religious monument on Earth and appears on its national flag.
It borders Thailand, Laos, and Vietnam and was heavily bombed by the US during the Vietnam War era.
medium: The Khmer Rouge regime, led by Pol Pot, committed genocide here between 1975 and 1979.
Angkor Wat, its most famous landmark, was built in the 12th century as a Hindu temple.
The Mekong River flows through this country, supporting agriculture for millions.
easy: Angkor Wat, the world's largest religious monument, is located here.
It is a small country in Southeast Asia.
Its flag is the only national flag in the world featuring a building.

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.didYouKnow: Ecuador was the first country in the world to grant rights to nature in its constitution, in 2008.

hard: This country's name literally translates to 'equator' in Spanish, as the geographic line runs through it.
It was the first country in the world to grant constitutional rights to nature.
Due to its equatorial bulge, the summit of its volcano Chimborazo is the point on Earth farthest from the planet's core — farther than Everest.
medium: The Galápagos Islands, which inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution, belong to this country.
It is the world's largest exporter of bananas.
It uses the US dollar as its official currency despite being an independent nation.
easy: The Galápagos Islands, famous for their unique wildlife, are part of this country.
It is named after the equator, which passes directly through it.
It is a small South American country bordered by Colombia and Peru.

countries.name: Ghana
countries.didYouKnow: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule, in 1957.

hard: This country was the first sub-Saharan African nation to gain independence from colonial rule, in 1957.
Its Ashanti kingdom was one of West Africa's most powerful pre-colonial states, known for its gold and Kente cloth.
Lake Volta, created by the Akosombo Dam, is one of the world's largest man-made lakes by area.
medium: It is the world's second largest producer of cocoa beans.
Its historical name, the Gold Coast, reflected the enormous gold wealth that attracted European traders.
Its capital is Accra, and it is considered one of Africa's most stable democracies.
easy: It is a West African country known for its political stability and cocoa production.
It was the first African country south of the Sahara to gain independence.
Its flag features three horizontal stripes of red, gold, and green with a black star.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.didYouKnow: Jordan hosts one of the highest numbers of refugees per capita in the world, mainly from Syria, Palestine, and Iraq.

hard: This country contains the Dead Sea, the lowest point on Earth's surface and the world's saltiest large body of water.
Its ancient rose-red city, carved directly into cliff faces, is considered one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
It is a constitutional monarchy that has maintained relative stability despite being surrounded by conflict.
medium: The ancient Nabataean city of Petra, carved from pink sandstone, is its most visited landmark.
The Dead Sea, on its western border, is so salty that swimmers float without effort.
It borders Israel, Syria, Iraq, and Saudi Arabia, and has peace treaties with two of them.
easy: The ancient city of Petra, with its rose-red stone facades, is located here.
The Dead Sea, the lowest point on Earth, is on its border.
It is a small Middle Eastern kingdom.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.didYouKnow: The University of Al-Qarawiyyin in Morocco, founded in 859 AD, is the world's oldest continuously operating university.

hard: This country is the only African nation with coastlines on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.
Its city of Fez contains the world's oldest continuously operating university, founded in 859 AD.
It controls over 70% of the world's proven phosphate reserves.
medium: Its famous medinas — ancient walled city centres — are UNESCO-listed and easy to get lost in.
The Sahara Desert begins at its southern edge.
Casablanca is its largest city, but Rabat is its capital — made famous by a classic Hollywood film.
easy: It is located at the northwestern tip of Africa, just across the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain.
Marrakech, with its famous souks and Djemaa el-Fna square, is one of its most visited cities.
Its flag is red with a green pentagram (five-pointed star) in the centre.

countries.name: Myanmar
countries.didYouKnow: Myanmar uses its own unique calendar system and time zone — UTC+6:30 — one of the few countries with a half-hour offset.

hard: This country uses a unique time zone — UTC+6:30 — making it one of the rare nations with a 30-minute offset.
It was under military dictatorship for most of its post-independence history, including a coup in 2021.
It is the world's largest producer of rubies and jade.

easy: It is a Southeast Asian country formerly known as Burma.
It has been under military rule for much of its history.
Thousands of ancient Buddhist pagodas fill the plains of Bagan.

countries.name: Peru
countries.didYouKnow: Peru is considered the origin of the potato — over 3,000 varieties are grown there, far more than anywhere else on Earth.

hard: This country was the heart of the Inca Empire, the largest pre-Columbian empire in the Americas.
It is the origin of the potato and home to over 3,000 native varieties of it.
Lake Titicaca, on its border, was believed by the Inca to be the birthplace of the sun.
medium: The ancient Inca citadel of Machu Picchu, set high in the Andes, is one of the world's most iconic archaeological sites.

Its cuisine is considered one of the most sophisticated in the world, blending indigenous and immigrant traditions.
easy: Machu Picchu, the ancient Inca mountaintop city, is located here.

The Amazon River originates from its Andes mountains.

countries.name: Bhutan
countries.didYouKnow: Bhutan measures its success not by GDP but by Gross National Happiness — an index it invented and the world has adopted in various forms.

hard: This country measures societal success using Gross National Happiness rather than GDP.
It is the only carbon-negative country in the world — it absorbs more CO₂ than it produces.

medium: It is a tiny Buddhist kingdom landlocked between India and China in the eastern Himalayas.

Its national animal is the takin — a bizarre creature that looks like a cross between a wildebeest and a goat.
easy: It is a small Himalayan kingdom famous for measuring Gross National Happiness.
It is one of the least visited countries in the world.
Its flag features a white dragon on a divided orange and yellow background.

countries.name: Djibouti
countries.didYouKnow: Djibouti hosts military bases from the United States, France, China, Japan, and Italy — more foreign military presences than any other country.

hard: This tiny country hosts military bases from more foreign nations than any other country in the world.
Lake Assal, on its territory, is the lowest point in Africa and the third lowest on Earth.

medium: It is one of the smallest countries in Africa, about the size of Massachusetts.

easy: It is a tiny country in the Horn of Africa.
It sits at the entrance to the Red Sea, across from Yemen.
Its capital city shares its name with the country itself.

countries.name: Eritrea
countries.didYouKnow: Eritrea has mandatory national service with no set end date — some citizens have served for over 20 years.

hard: This country has mandatory national service with no legal end date, effectively making it indefinite.
Its capital city has the largest collection of modernist Art Deco architecture in the world, built during Italian colonization.

medium: It is one of the most isolated and closed countries in the world, often compared to North Korea.

easy: It is a small East African country on the Red Sea coast.

countries.name: Kiribati
countries.didYouKnow: Kiribati is the only country in the world to span all four hemispheres simultaneously.

hard: This country is the only one in the world that spans all four hemispheres — north, south, east, and west.
It is one of the first countries that will disappear due to rising sea levels — most of its land sits less than 2 metres above sea level.
It crosses the International Date Line, meaning it has the same calendar date in places separated by 3,000 kilometres.
medium: It is made up of 33 atolls scattered across the central Pacific Ocean.
Its name is pronounced 'Kiribas' — the 'ti' in its language sounds like 's.'
It has no high ground — its highest point is only about 3 metres above sea level.
easy: It is a tiny Pacific island nation at risk of disappearing due to climate change.
It is one of the least-known countries in the world.
Its name is pronounced 'Kiribas.'

countries.name: Turkmenistan
countries.didYouKnow: Turkmenistan has the fourth largest natural gas reserves in the world, yet most of its population lives in poverty.

hard: This country contains a massive burning gas crater in the middle of its desert, nicknamed the 'Door to Hell,' which has been on fire since 1971.
Its former dictator renamed months of the year and days of the week after himself and his family members.

medium: It is one of the world's most repressive and secretive states, with extremely restricted access for foreigners.

easy: It is a reclusive former Soviet republic in Central Asia.
